{"world_model":"W6 model after E051. Time ≈ 0.1 s fixed + steps × per-step cost. Per-step cost = pixel-proportional compute + a bandwidth-bound part (BN/GELU/pointwise, ~27% of a 32 px step). Tip E049: 5.198 s, 0.7535 on seeds 0–2. The population mean is ~0.752, only ~0.2 pp over the bar. Rebuilds of the same commit read 0.7525–0.7552 (E036 vs E050), so differences under 0.3 pp on 3 seeds are noise.

Mechanisms and support:
1. Accuracy rises slowly with optimizer steps, about 1.5–2.5 s/pp. Pure step, epoch and sample cuts trade at dial-like rates (E020, E031, E040, E041, E037, E045, E048). Loss-based selection is roughly dial-neutral.
2. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
3. Late backward truncation saves more than its MAC share, because frozen blocks also skip BN/GELU backward, optimizer updates and Lookahead traffic. Support: E028, E034, E036, E046, E049. Late freezes are roughly neutral; early ones are not (E037's cliff). Each added freeze yields ~0.1–0.2 s. Extending group 2's freeze dose (I082) should give a further ~0.05–0.1 s at ~0.05–0.1 pp cost.
4. Averaging, LS, warm-up, Lookahead-interval, BN-recalibration and batch-split tweaks are null or negative (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, E045). The recipe is near a local optimum.
5. Math-identical systems work is worth 1–2% each (E035). Only ~2.5% of GPU time is outside the step graphs (E047).
6. wd ×0.5 helped ~0.2 pp (E016).
7. Architecture surgery that changes the stem (E051: stride-2 conv replacing conv+pool) saved 0.29 s (-5.6%) but cost 0.9 pp. That is a time-for-accuracy rate of ~0.3 s/pp, far worse than the dial. Architecture cuts of high-res work lose accuracy faster than they save time.
8. Elementwise work is bytes-bound. ReLU should save 1–3% of time, with an accuracy effect of -0.1 to -0.3 pp, since GELU is smoother and the recipe is tuned for it.
9. Build-to-build kernel reselection moves 3-seed accuracy by up to ~0.3 pp. Time noise is ±0.04 s.

Misses: truncation and selection savings beat my estimates (E041, E046, E048). Accuracy swung ±0.3 pp on identical code. E051's accuracy miss was on the low side: an architecture change costs far more than the noise. Lesson: use wide accuracy ranges, but expect real architecture changes to lose several tenths of a pp.

Tip E049: 5.198 s, 0.7535 on seeds 0–2. The population mean is ~0.752, only ~0.2 pp over the bar. Rebuilds of the same commit read 0.7525–0.7552 (E036 vs E050), so differences under 0.3 pp on 3 seeds are noise.

Mechanisms and support:
1. Accuracy rises slowly with optimizer steps, about 1.5–2.5 s/pp. Pure step, epoch and sample cuts trade at dial-like rates (E020, E031, E040, E041, E037, E045, E048). Loss-based selection is roughly dial-neutral.
2. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
3. Late backward truncation saves more than its MAC share, because frozen blocks also skip BN/GELU backward, optimizer updates and Lookahead traffic. Support: E028, E034, E036, E046, E049. Late freezes are roughly neutral; early ones are not (E037's cliff). Each added freeze yields ~0.1–0.2 s. Extending group 2's freeze dose (I082) should give a further ~0.05–0.1 s at ~0.05–0.1 pp cost.
4. Averaging, LS, warm-up, Lookahead-interval, BN-recalibration and batch-split tweaks are null or negative (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, E045). The recipe is near a local optimum.
5. Math-identical systems work is worth 1–2% each (E035). Only ~2.5% of GPU time is outside the step graphs (E047).
6. wd ×0.5 helped ~0.2 pp (E016).
7. Architecture surgery that changes the stem (E051: stride-2 conv replacing conv+pool) saved 0.29 s (-5.6%) but cost 0.9 pp. That is a time-for-accuracy rate of ~0.3 s/pp, far worse than the dial. Architecture cuts of high-res work lose accuracy faster than they save time.
8. Elementwise work is bytes-bound. ReLU should save 1–3% of time, with an accuracy effect of -0.1 to -0.3 pp, since GELU is smoother and the recipe is tuned for it.

E051's accuracy miss was on the low side: an architecture change costs far more than the noise. Lesson: use wide accuracy ranges, but expect real architecture changes to lose several tenths of a pp.

Unsure: the true tip mean (0.752 ± 0.1), the selection bias, transfer to the PCIe judge, how far the group-2 freeze can extend, and whether activation swaps are neutral.

forecasts.reason: ReLU saves a little bandwidth/erf time; accuracy likely slightly lower, within noise at 3 seeds.
Selection plus top-up nets to about the dial; net steps about the same as the tip, so time and accuracy are near the tip's.
A longer group-2 freeze saves ~0.06 s with a small possible accuracy cost, hard to resolve at 3 seeds.

cruxes: Does the group-2 freeze plus top-up (E049) hold at about 0.752 on a 20-seed unselected mean against same-build E036? That decides whether freezes are still free.
